-- | A Haskell-to-Verilog/VHDL compiler, shared base utilities
--   
--   The shared foundation for the ReWire compiler. Source annotations
--   (ReWire.Annotation), bit vectors, the Config and Flags records,
--   diagnostics (ReWire.Error), pretty-printing, and the SYB and
--   orphan-instance glue. Consumed by rewire-backend and rewire-frontend.
@package rewire-base
@version 2.8

module ReWire.BitVector
data BV
width :: BV -> Int
ones :: Int -> BV
zeros :: Int -> BV
nil :: BV
(@@) :: Integral ix => BV -> (ix, ix) -> BV
bitVec :: Integral a => Int -> a -> BV
(>>.) :: BV -> BV -> BV
(<<.) :: BV -> BV -> BV
(==.) :: BV -> BV -> Bool
ashr :: BV -> BV -> BV
replicate :: Integral size => size -> BV -> BV
lsb1 :: BV -> Int
(@.) :: Integral ix => BV -> ix -> Bool
concat :: [BV] -> BV

-- | Show the bitvec value in hex, with "0x" prefix, but no leading zeros.
showHex :: BV -> Text

-- | Like <a>showHex</a>, but prefix with <tt>h</tt> instead of `0x`.
showHex' :: BV -> Text

-- | Number of bits needed to encode <tt>n</tt> different values: exact
--   integer ceil-log2 via clog2(n) = 1 + clog2(ceil(n/2)) (floating-point
--   logBase mis-rounds near powers of two once n exceeds 2^29 or so).
nbits :: Natural -> Natural

-- | Number of bits in the binary representation of <tt>n</tt> (with no
--   leading zeros).
szBitRep :: Natural -> Natural

-- | <i>O(1).</i> A Builder taking a <tt>String</tt>, satisfying

--   <ul>

-- | An associative operation.
--   
--   <h4><b>Examples</b></h4>
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; [1,2,3] &lt;&gt; [4,5,6]

--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; Just [1, 2, 3] &lt;&gt; Just [4, 5, 6]

module ReWire.SYB
data Tr (m :: Type -> Type) a
TId :: Tr (m :: Type -> Type) a
TM :: (a -> m a) -> Tr (m :: Type -> Type) a
T :: (a -> a) -> Tr (m :: Type -> Type) a
transformTr :: (Data a, Data b, Monad m) => Tr m a -> b -> m b
transform :: (Data a, Data b) => (a -> a) -> b -> b
transformM :: (Monad m, Data a, Data b) => (a -> m a) -> b -> m b
query :: (Data a, Data b) => a -> [b]

-- | A query in a single generic sweep: collects <tt>f b</tt> at every node
--   of type <tt>b</tt>. Unlike <a>query</a> at an expression type, it
--   never re-extracts a node's children per level, which is quadratic on
--   deeply nested binders.
queryWith :: (Data a, Typeable b) => (b -> [r]) -> a -> [r]

-- | A generic transformation that maps over the immediate subterms
--   
--   The default definition instantiates the type constructor <tt>c</tt> in
--   the type of <a>gfoldl</a> to an identity datatype constructor, using
--   the isomorphism pair as injection and projection.
gmapT :: Data a => (forall b. Data b => b -> b) -> a -> a
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Monad m => GHC.Internal.Base.Monoid (ReWire.SYB.Tr m a)
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Monad m => GHC.Internal.Base.Semigroup (ReWire.SYB.Tr m a)

module ReWire.Annotation

-- | The annotation carried by every IR node: its provenance plus any
--   human-readable context breadcrumbs accumulated as it travels through
--   the passes.
data Annote
Annote :: !Provenance -> ![Text] -> Annote

-- | The empty annotation: a node with no known origin.
pattern NoAnnote :: Annote

-- | A locationless annotation carrying a single explanatory message.
--   Matches the first context message of any annotation.
pattern MsgAnnote :: Text -> Annote

-- | Where an annotated node came from. Nodes parsed from user source are
--   <a>FromSource</a>; nodes a pass invents are <a>Synthesized</a>,
--   recording the pass name and the source spans of the inputs it was
--   built from (so errors on generated code can still point back at the
--   user's source).
data Provenance
FromSource :: !Span -> Provenance
Synthesized :: !Text -> ![Span] -> Provenance
NoProvenance :: Provenance

-- | A source region: a file together with 1-based (line, column) start and
--   end positions. Carries the full extent of a node (unlike a single
--   point), which is what lets a diagnostic underline the offending text.
data Span
Span :: !FilePath -> !(Int, Int) -> !(Int, Int) -> Span
[spanFile] :: Span -> !FilePath
[spanStart] :: Span -> !(Int, Int)
[spanEnd] :: Span -> !(Int, Int)
class Annotation a
toAnnote :: Annotation a => a -> Annote
class Annotated a
ann :: Annotated a => a -> Annote

-- | Display metadata invisible to equality, ordering, and hashing:
--   wrapping a field in <a>Blind</a> keeps doc lines and tag tables from
--   perturbing dedupe keys, memo keys, or the optimizer's fixpoint test
--   (the same convention as <a>Annote</a> itself, for metadata that isn't
--   an annotation).
newtype Blind a
Blind :: a -> Blind a
[unBlind] :: Blind a -> a

-- | Build an annotation for an explicit source region: a file with 1-based
--   (line, column) start and end positions.
srcAnnote :: FilePath -> (Int, Int) -> (Int, Int) -> Annote

-- | The source span underlying an annotation, if it has one. Synthesized
--   nodes yield the span of their first input.
primSpan :: Annote -> Maybe Span
annProv :: Annote -> Provenance
annContext :: Annote -> [Text]
noAnn :: Annote

-- | Strip every annotation from a value, replacing each with <a>noAnn</a>.
--   Used to make dumps readable and to compare terms structurally.
unAnn :: Data d => d -> d
instance ReWire.Annotation.Annotation ReWire.Annotation.Annote
instance GHC.Internal.Data.Data.Data ReWire.Annotation.Annote
instance GHC.Internal.Data.Data.Data a => GHC.Internal.Data.Data.Data (ReWire.Annotation.Blind a)
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.Annotation.Annote
instance GHC.Classes.Eq (ReWire.Annotation.Blind a)
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.Annotation.Provenance
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.Annotation.Span
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic (ReWire.Annotation.Blind a)
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic ReWire.Annotation.Provenance
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic ReWire.Annotation.Span
instance Data.Hashable.Class.Hashable ReWire.Annotation.Annote
instance Data.Hashable.Class.Hashable (ReWire.Annotation.Blind a)
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData ReWire.Annotation.Annote
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData a => Control.DeepSeq.NFData (ReWire.Annotation.Blind a)
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData ReWire.Annotation.Provenance
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData ReWire.Annotation.Span
instance GHC.Classes.Ord ReWire.Annotation.Annote
instance GHC.Classes.Ord (ReWire.Annotation.Blind a)
instance GHC.Classes.Ord ReWire.Annotation.Provenance
instance GHC.Classes.Ord ReWire.Annotation.Span
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.Annotation.Annote
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show a => GHC.Internal.Show.Show (ReWire.Annotation.Blind a)
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.Annotation.Provenance
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.Annotation.Span
instance TextShow.Classes.TextShow ReWire.Annotation.Annote
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show a => TextShow.Classes.TextShow (ReWire.Annotation.Blind a)

module ReWire.Error

-- | The point of the newtype and all the annoying boilerplate is to
--   redefine the "fail" method of the Monad and MonadFail typeclasses.
data SyntaxErrorT ex (m :: Type -> Type) a

-- | An error: a primary location and message, plus optional secondary
--   labelled locations and suggested-fix hints.
data AstError

-- | A non-fatal diagnostic: printed to stderr when emitted (see
--   <a>warnAt</a>), or promoted to an <a>AstError</a> under -Werror.
data Warning
Warning :: !Annote -> !Text -> Warning

-- | A secondary location with an explanatory note, attached to an error to
--   point at a related part of the source (e.g. "first defined here").
type Label = (Annote, Text)

-- | The strategy of combining computations that can throw exceptions by
--   bypassing bound functions from the point an exception is thrown to the
--   point that it is handled.
--   
--   Is parameterized over the type of error information and the monad type
--   constructor. It is common to use <tt><a>Either</a> String</tt> as the
--   monad type constructor for an error monad in which error descriptions
--   take the form of strings. In that case and many other common cases the
--   resulting monad is already defined as an instance of the
--   <a>MonadError</a> class. You can also define your own error type
--   and/or use a monad type constructor other than <tt><a>Either</a>
--   <tt>String</tt></tt> or <tt><a>Either</a> <tt>IOError</tt></tt>. In
--   these cases you will have to explicitly define instances of the
--   <a>MonadError</a> class. (If you are using the deprecated
--   <a>Control.Monad.Error</a> or <a>Control.Monad.Trans.Error</a>, you
--   may also have to define an <tt>Error</tt> instance.)
class Monad m => MonadError e (m :: Type -> Type) | m -> e
mark :: (MonadState AstError m, Annotation an) => an -> m ()
failAt :: (MonadError AstError m, Annotation an) => an -> Text -> m a

-- | Like failAt, but include an extra bit of data on failure.
failAt' :: (MonadError (ex, AstError) m, Annotation an) => ex -> an -> Text -> m a

-- | Like <a>failAt</a>, but attach secondary labelled locations and/or
--   hints.
failAtWith :: (MonadError AstError m, Annotation an) => an -> Text -> [Label] -> [Text] -> m a

-- | Report a violated internal invariant: a bug in rwc itself, not a
--   problem with the user's program. Rendered with a "please report it"
--   hint so the message can't be mistaken for a complaint about the user's
--   code.
failInternal :: (MonadError AstError m, Annotation an) => an -> Text -> m a

-- | Re-point a diagnostic at a fallback location when it has none, or when
--   it resolves to a different source file than the fallback — typically
--   because the error surfaced inside inlined library code while compiling
--   a user definition. The original location, when it had one, is kept as
--   a secondary note so the expansion site stays visible.
relocateErr :: Annotation an => an -> AstError -> AstError

-- | Run an action, relocating any error it raises to the given fallback
--   location (see <a>relocateErr</a>).
relocatingTo :: (MonadError AstError m, Annotation an) => an -> m a -> m a
relocatingNoLocTo :: (MonadError AstError m, Annotation an) => an -> m a -> m a
failNowhere :: (PutMsg ex, Monad m, MonadState ex m, MonadError ex m) => Text -> m a

-- | Emit a warning: printed to stderr immediately (so it isn't lost if a
--   later pass fails), suppressed by -w, or promoted to an error by
--   -Werror (which therefore fails on the *first* warning).
warnAt :: (MonadError AstError m, MonadIO m, Annotation an) => Config -> an -> Text -> m ()
filePath :: FilePath -> Annote

-- | Print an error to stderr, GHC-style, with a source excerpt and a caret
--   under the offending region (plus any secondary "note" blocks) when the
--   files can be found on the load path.
printError :: MonadIO m => [FilePath] -> AstError -> m ()
runSyntaxError :: Monad m => SyntaxErrorT AstError m a -> m (Either AstError a)
class PutMsg a
putMsg :: PutMsg a => Text -> a -> a
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Monad m => GHC.Internal.Base.Applicative (ReWire.Error.SyntaxErrorT ex m)
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.Error.Warning
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Functor m => GHC.Internal.Base.Functor (ReWire.Error.SyntaxErrorT ex m)
instance Control.Monad.Catch.MonadCatch m => Control.Monad.Catch.MonadCatch (ReWire.Error.SyntaxErrorT ex m)
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Monad m => Control.Monad.Error.Class.MonadError ex (ReWire.Error.SyntaxErrorT ex m)
instance (ReWire.Error.PutMsg ex, GHC.Internal.Base.Monad m) => GHC.Internal.Control.Monad.Fail.MonadFail (ReWire.Error.SyntaxErrorT ex m)
instance Control.Monad.IO.Class.MonadIO m => Control.Monad.IO.Class.MonadIO (ReWire.Error.SyntaxErrorT ex m)
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Monad m => Control.Monad.State.Class.MonadState ex (ReWire.Error.SyntaxErrorT ex m)
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Monad m => GHC.Internal.Base.Monad (ReWire.Error.SyntaxErrorT ex m)
instance Control.Monad.Catch.MonadThrow m => Control.Monad.Catch.MonadThrow (ReWire.Error.SyntaxErrorT ex m)
instance Control.Monad.Trans.Class.MonadTrans (ReWire.Error.SyntaxErrorT ex)
instance GHC.Classes.Ord ReWire.Error.Warning
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.Error.AstError
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.Error.Warning
instance ReWire.Error.PutMsg ReWire.Error.AstError

module ReWire.Fix
fix :: (MonadError AstError m, Hashable a) => Text -> Natural -> (a -> m a) -> a -> m a
fix' :: Hashable a => (a -> a) -> a -> a
fixOn :: (MonadError AstError m, Eq b) => (a -> b) -> Text -> Natural -> (a -> m a) -> a -> m a

-- | Note: evaluates `(f a)` at least once if the bound is not reached.
boundedFixOn :: MonadError AstError m => (a -> a -> Bool) -> Text -> Natural -> (a -> m a) -> a -> m a

-- | Note: the recursive call must reuse the already-forced <tt>f a</tt> --
--   passing the expression <tt>f a</tt> itself builds an unshared thunk
--   chain that gets re-evaluated from scratch at every level, making the
--   fixpoint exponential in the iteration count.
fixOn' :: Eq b => (a -> b) -> (a -> a) -> a -> a
fixUntil :: MonadError AstError m => (a -> Bool) -> Text -> Natural -> (a -> m a) -> a -> m a
boundedFix :: Monad m => (a -> a -> Bool) -> Natural -> (a -> m a) -> a -> m a

-- | Note: direct equality rather than comparing hashes: equality can stop
--   at the first difference, while hashing always traverses both terms
--   fully.
fixPure :: Eq a => Natural -> (a -> a) -> a -> a


-- | Pure SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4), used to bind validator responses to the
--   exact artifact bytes they were computed from. Self-contained so rwc
--   carries no cryptography dependency for the sake of one digest.
module ReWire.Sha256

-- | The lowercase hex SHA-256 digest of a byte string.
hashHex :: ByteString -> Text
